item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers facet-selective Li₂CO₃ growth in Li-CO₂ batteries via a MoS₂@CuS heterointerface that induces a 2H-to-1T phase transition. The 1T phase preferentially stabilizes Li₂CO₃ (−110) facets, lowering decomposition barriers and enabling oriented epitaxial growth. This yields low overpotential (0.46 V), ~92.4% efficiency, and >1800 h cycling, linking catalyst structure, interfacial interactions, and product crystallography.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers in situ solvent polymerization in ether electrolytes, using trace LiPF₆ to trigger DOL ring-opening and form PDOL, which reconstructs Na⁺ solvation. This simultaneously enables fast ion transport and stable interphase, overcoming the traditional trade-off. The strategy yields high capacity retention in both coin and pouch sodium-ion cells, offering a viable design pathway for high-performance electrolytes.

item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work reveals that low-temperature ion transport in sodium-ion battery electrolytes is governed by ion-association dynamics, not static solvation structures. By combining machine-learned molecular dynamics with variable-temperature Raman spectroscopy, it shows cooling prolongs ion-pair lifetimes and suppresses reorganization, reducing fast-migrating Na+. This mechanistic insight offers a new design principle for low-temperature electrolytes.

💡 This work uniquely links cathode microstructure to fracture in solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries via a resolved electro-chemo-mechanical framework. It reveals that constrained conversion expansion creates strain-energy hotspots governing crack morphology, and identifies sulfur particle size and packing density as key design levers. These insights expose an energy density–mechanical stability trade-off, offering a mechanistic basis for durable electrode design.
